static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.educational_background: In the second year of medical school
static_traits.family_status: Having two children; mother is known for baking skills, relationship is supportive
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive mother and friends, but has not shared the self-doubt with them; relationships with colleagues are affected by self-criticism
static_traits.medical_history: No notable physical illness; no previous similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic; tone rather negative, often self-deprecating; frequently compares with others; able to cooperate in exploration; skeptical attitude toward change

basic_info.main_problem: I believe the reason I am in my second year of medical school is that I am not smart enough to complete the studies in one year, which leads to self-doubt and inferiority.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to increase confidence in their own abilities, stop feeling inferior to others, and be able to focus on studying without persistent self-doubt; sought help because these thoughts affect academic performance and overall well-being.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on grades and progress

special_situations.event: During exams or when others announce academic results
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get a high score or progress faster, it proves my ability is insufficient
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Compares with others, belittles own grades, and imposes higher and more rigid demands on the self
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not cut out for studying medicine; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When peers announce high scores or appear to be progressing faster academically
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others perform better, it means I am bad and falling behind
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces positive interaction with peers and avoids seeking help from supporters lest it appear weak
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone is faster and smarter than me; I have fallen behind

special_situations.event: Gaining professor praise in lab class or performing well in some exams
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If it is not perfect or top-level, it does not count as real ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attributing success to luck or low standards, deliberately ignoring positive evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count; I barely passed

special_situations.event: Realizing one is in the second year of medical school (not finishing faster)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete it within a year, it proves I am not smart enough, not worthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using self-labeling to explain the current situation, continuing to raise standards to push oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The reason I am in the second year is that I am not smart enough

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and accepted as a capable, respected professional
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being compared and judged as not good enough, thus being negated or excluded
defense_goal: Avoiding external blows through self-criticism and lowering expectations
Hiding vulnerability (not confiding in family and friends) to avoid being seen as weak

object_relations.object_representation: More capable and judgmental peers or authorities

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor focuses on their achievements, invites them to identify strengths, or gives positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes positive feedback 'does not count', or worries about being expected of and being exposed as 'actually not good enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle tone and validate feelings, avoiding confrontational persuasion; use open-ended questions and concretization techniques, inviting examples of their actual achievements and evidence; use a slow pace with pauses to help them stay with the affirmed experience.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about whether to express self-doubt to mother or friends and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing vulnerability will be seen as weakness and may lead to being looked down on or rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintains an empathic and safe atmosphere, uses gentle invitational language; allows them to share at a bearable pace, emphasizing choice and self-direction.

manifestations: Completely equates self-worth with grades and study progress
Even when achieving results or being praised, still feels it 'does not count'
Constantly comparing with others, devaluing one's own significance
Although having a support system (mother and friends), not sharing real feelings
Worrying about appearing weak and avoiding seeking help
outcomes: Reduced subjective sense of support, increased emotional burden

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Internalizes others' standards of 'must finish faster, must get high scores to count as good' as the sole yardstick for judging their own value
Uses progress and scores as the absolute basis of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally directed outward onto the self, restraining impulses or no longer seeking help outwardly.
manifestations: Knowing there is a supportive mother and friends, still choosing not to express and not to seek help
When in self-doubt, 'enduring it', turning criticism and pressure toward oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Persistent self-criticism, worried about appearing weak
Staying skeptical of positive feedback, difficulty accepting it

exception_events.target_problem: In situations such as exams or the release of peer grades, the client usually engages in self-negation and comparison, leading to inferiority and reduced concentration.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Achieved good performance in certain exams and practical operations, and received praise from the professor in the lab class; at the time the client could engage more fully in completing tasks, with better results than before.
exception_events.reason: Clues: received positive feedback from the professor (different support); the experimental skills context better matched their strengths (different context), so confidence and engagement relatively increased.

exception_events.target_problem: When facing academic pressure and comparison with others, the client usually ignores their own strengths and negates positive evidence.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once tried to focus on their own strengths and achievements and could list concrete experiences of being praised by professors, loosening somewhat compared with the usual complete self-negation.
exception_events.reason: Cue: deliberately thinking about and recalling successful experiences (different approaches), making positive evidence more visible.

positive_force: Has a supportive mother and friends
Positive performance in labs and some exams, and praise from professors
Willing to seek help and start counseling; willing to try small goals
Able to identify some negative thinking patterns
negative_force: Avoidance of vulnerability and help-seeking (worried about being seen as weak)
Sleep disturbance and impaired concentration amplify the negative cycle

antecedent: When an exam is approaching or in progress
When hearing peers announce high scores or faster progress
Thinking about when one was in the second year
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly binds self-worth to grades / progress, with the inner core belief 'I am not smart enough'; long-term comparison with others reinforces negative evaluation
target_behavior.function: Gains control in the short term and lowers others' expectations, avoiding uncertainty and the anxiety of being judged
target_behavior.consequence: Academic performance and confidence are impaired, attention declines, sleep is disturbed, and relationships with peers are affected

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding seeking social support (not expressing troubles to mother and friends)
antecedent: When strong self-doubt or inferiority arises
When low after comparing with peers
target_behavior.core_reason: Worried about being seen as weak or judged, producing feelings of shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential negation and shame experiences, maintaining a sense of self-protection in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Subjective sense of support decreases, emotional burden accumulates, negative beliefs are maintained
